shots.text: Three hundred twenty ants in my colony.
shots.note: Wide: the amber tunnels, hundreds of identical trap-jaws.
A pale new ant unfolds among the brood.

shots.text: Not first, not last, just... in the middle.
shots.note: A single-file line; 250 is the one in the middle.

shots.text: The first ants born get names, stories, a place near the queen.
shots.note: The queen's chamber, the first-born at her side.

shots.text: The ones in the middle get nothing.
shots.note: Back to the line; nobody looks at the middle.

shots.text: In the nursery tunnels, nobody learned my name because I didn't have one.
When the soldiers marched past, I stepped aside without being asked.
shots.note: Big soldiers march by; 250 presses himself against the wall.

shots.text: I was good at being invisible. Too good.
Sometimes I wondered if I'd disappear completely and nobody would even count the difference.
shots.note: Pull back; 250 slowly fades out of the crowd.

shots.text: Then one morning, out past the root wall, where young ants aren't supposed to go,
shots.note: Dawn light through a wall of giant roots; 250 walks out alone.

shots.text: I stepped in something that glowed.
shots.note: The green amoeba at his feet.
